decision: Use one fail-closed operational command that runs duration-bound calibration for every candidate topology and immediately feeds the resulting measured reports into the existing calibrated topology evaluator.

reviews.correctness: Preferred one authority because manual handoff can mix stale or wrong-SHA calibration reports with candidate definitions. Require one report per candidate and exact topology/SHA provenance before evaluation.
reviews.robustness_security: Preferred fail-closed provenance and no-winner behavior. The command does not weaken qrexec, attestation, workload cleanup, or resource gates and performs no financial or external side effects.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Preferred composition of existing duration-bound calibration and evaluator modules. It adds no calibration probes beyond those already required and only adds local validation/evaluation overhead. A new daemon/database or a second benchmark pass was rejected as higher resource and regression cost.

alternatives_rejected: Manual calibration then manual topology evaluation: vulnerable to stale/mismatched evidence and operator drift.
New telemetry daemon/database: unnecessary lifecycle, credentials, resource use, and attack surface.
Second Qubes benchmark solely for selection: extra qrexec/CPU cost without improving the already measured resource/probe-latency evidence.
qa: Run calibration once per candidate topology.
Reject wrong SHA, unexpected topology, mismatched returned report provenance, and missing candidate calibration.
Reject qualification when no candidate satisfies the evaluator gates.
Preserve duration-bound observed timing as the calibration authority.
lesson: Measured evidence is only useful when the operational path consumes it without a manual provenance gap.
